Bayes chapter quality audit

State: passed within the recorded verification domains; review draft awaiting the user's explicit approval. Date: 2026-10-04.

Delivered content and editorial review

The English chapter develops partition normalization, countable hypotheses, Bayes, likelihood scale, zero-evidence boundaries, natural frequencies, base rates, odds, history-dependent updates, independent versus copied reports, fixed versus redrawn latent state, prediction, host/report protocols, prior sensitivity, inverse feasibility, decision risk, and an elementary continuous-density bridge. Derivations include the sign of an evidence update, monotone response and threshold inequalities, posterior-risk thresholds, and the integer beta-integral proof. The final summary connects these results; 80 complete rules explain formula use and failure cases.

The bank contains 65 worked questions: two checked authentic archive revisits and 63 original/course-derived medium-to-hard mathematical/conceptual problems. Numerical and conceptual tasks include posterior vectors, inverse rates, countable normalization, repeated-evidence thresholds, without-replacement likelihoods, latent predictive mixtures, size bias, host policy, bounds, costs, polynomial integrals and null-event limits. Source-inspired questions identify their origin. No source exercise is silently described as an authentic Iranian examination item.

Exact mathematical and structural checks

verify_s_bayes_en.py passed 7,446 assertions. Its domains include the complete 9-by-9-by-9 rational prior/likelihood grid, boundary impossible-evidence models, posterior normalization and odds identities, sharp threshold equivalence, the 81 integer head/tail integral pairs from zero through eight, direct enumeration of the four-coin second-round experiment, and independent urn/pair-selection counts. Seventy-three explicit selected numerical-answer occurrences are bound to independently computed results in the manuscript. Source and booklet fingerprints, native MathML well-formedness, 65 solution containers, 80 rules, seven figures, ten simulations, and preservation of all 24 prior approvals are checked.

The ten new simulations contain 51 exact checkpoints. Their serialized masses, posterior values, host likelihoods, risk values, density integrals and sampled density heights receive independent rational checks. General library state/reference checks passed 3,572 assertions across 124 models and 808 checkpoints. These counts describe assertions, not independent theorems or a probability of correctness.

Rendered-page and interaction review

qa_bayes_browser.py passed local Edge desktop, 390-pixel mobile and print checks. Seven figures were captured and all their labels checked for clipping and text overlap. Mathematical runs and figure labels use STIX Two Math; body text uses Source Sans 3, headings Newsreader and code JetBrains Mono. Every solution opens for printing and returns to its prior state afterward. Links have no underline. Two initially oversized formula rows were rewritten with proper fractions; no formula or document overflow remains in the measured viewport.

The exact laboratory passed five presets: rare positive, rare negative, two independent positives, copied positive and impossible report. Invalid fractions with zero denominator, negative input, out-of-range value, decimal notation, nonnumeric input and excessive denominator are rejected. Zero observations return the prior with evidence probability one. The calculation uses BigInt fractions, not rounded floating-point weights.

qa_animations_browser.py rendered all 124 models across 25 chapters and their checkpoints with zero text-layout findings. It also exercised playback, stepping, backward movement, seeking, restart, keyboard, speed, zoom, reduced-motion and print behavior. Prior problem entries and written approvals remain preserved. Detailed records: mathematical validation, chapter browser audit, and animation evidence.

Remaining limits

Proofs and explanations receive editorial derivation review; automated checks cover the stated finite domains and selected result bindings, not all symbolic claims for every possible input. The candidate-course pool is documented and bounded, with inaccessible courses excluded from the reading count. The bank samples chapter-relevant examination patterns and does not reproduce every university exercise or every archived exam item. Neither source selection nor finite simulation establishes literal universal coverage, perfect scientific accuracy, or a guaranteed score on all unseen questions. The user must explicitly approve this draft before another chapter begins.
